title: Deep Learning-Based Credit Risk Modeling: Addressing Data Imbalance and Invariance
venue: Journal of Trends in Financial and Economics
tldr: A deep learning framework integrating GAN-based data augmentation, adversarial fairness learning, and cost-sensitive classification improves credit risk prediction recall for high-risk borrowers by 22%.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional credit risk models struggle with class imbalance where defaulters are significantly underrepresented, leading to biased predictions favoring non-defaulters. Many existing models exhibit distributional bias where certain borrower groups receive systematically different credit scores due to dataset imbalances. Deep learning models also face challenges in maintaining fairness and stability across different demographic and economic conditions.
approach: Integrated framework combining autoencoders for feature learning, GANs for synthetic data generation, and adversarial training for fairness.
SMOTE-based oversampling and random undersampling rebalance class distributions while GAN augmentation generates realistic defaulter profiles.
Cost-sensitive learning assigns higher misclassification penalties for false negatives to improve sensitivity to high-risk borrowers.
Adversarial training with competing classifier and adversary enforces fairness constraints independent of demographic attributes.
Domain adaptation techniques ensure model stability across different economic conditions and borrower distributions.
Hybrid loss function balances classification accuracy, fairness constraints, and cost-sensitive penalties.
Evaluation using precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC, disparate impact ratios, and equality of opportunity metrics.
findings: num: GAN-based augmentation improves recall for high-risk borrowers by 22% while maintaining high precision.
num: Overall AUC-ROC score consistently higher across different credit datasets compared to traditional ML models.
Adversarial learning significantly reduced bias in risk assessments across borrower demographics.
Model maintained low latency inference processing thousands of borrower applications per second.
num: Scalability tests on 100,000 to 10 million transactions showed stable performance.
Transfer learning enabled fine-tuning on new datasets without requiring full retraining.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: Credit Risk Prediction Accuracy Comparison → DL framework outperforms traditional ML models across all metrics.
Figure 2: Impact of Data Augmentation → GAN and cost-sensitive learning reduce class imbalance effects.
Figure 3: Fairness in Credit Risk Scoring → Adversarial training reduces demographic bias in predictions.
Figure 4: Computational Efficiency → Model scales to millions of records with stable inference speed.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a unified deep learning framework that integrates GAN-based data augmentation, adversarial fairness learning, and cost-sensitive classification for credit risk modeling. It demonstrates that combining generative models with adversarial training significantly improves recall for high-risk borrowers while reducing demographic bias. The work addresses the critical gap in maintaining model invariance across different borrower segments through domain adaptation techniques. The framework provides a comprehensive solution balancing prediction accuracy, fairness, and computational efficiency for large-scale financial applications.
directly_justifies: GAN-based augmentation improves recall for high-risk borrowers by 22% over traditional methods.
Adversarial training reduces demographic bias in credit risk assessments.
Model scales to 10 million transactions with stable inference performance.
Cost-sensitive learning effectively reduces misclassified defaulters without increasing false positives.
limits: Computational cost of training GANs and adversarial networks on large-scale datasets is significant.
Deep learning models lack explainability required for regulatory compliance in credit decisions.
Experiments conducted on specific credit datasets may not generalize to all financial contexts.
No comparison with state-of-the-art transformer-based credit scoring models.

topic_relevance.topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) flagged 4.A as medium for reviewing traditional credit risk models and 4.B as high for identifying limitations in handling imbalance and invariance. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) flagged 6.A as high for the proposed DL-based framework. Domain 10 (Privacy) flagged 10.A as medium for addressing fairness and regulatory compliance. Domain 12 (Evaluation) flagged 12.A as medium for comprehensive evaluation metrics. Domains 1-3, 5, 7-9, 11, 13-14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, expense categorization, budgeting strategies, anomaly detection algorithms, mobile design, engagement, savings, debt management, or ML deployment specifics. The paper's topical coverage centers on predictive modeling for credit risk with emphasis on fairness and data augmentation techniques.
